title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ecuadorian Foreign Minister Roberto Kury Deliver Statements
text: hide Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ecuadorian Foreign Minister Roberto Kury Deliver Statements Remarks Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Roberto Kury Pesantes, Ecuadorian Foreign Minister of Human Mobility Palacio de Carondelet Quito, Ecuador September 10, 2026 MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We are receiving Secretary of State Marco Rubio from the United States of America, and also Roberto Kury Pesantes, the Foreign Minister of Ecuador. Ladies and gentlemen, dear authorities, representatives from the press that are here with us today, please, everybody be welcome to this joint press release on behalf of Secretary of State Marco Rubio from the United States of America and Roberto Kury Pesantes, Foreign Minister of Ecuador. In this space we will be able to share the main findings of this day. Now we would like to invite Foreign Minister Roberto Kury, Foreign Minister of Human Mobility of Ecuador. FOREIGN MINISTER KURY: (Via interpreter) Good afternoon to all of the representatives of the press that are here with us today. For us it’s an absolute honor to be hosting you and hosting the second official visit on behalf of the Secretary of State of the United States, Marco Rubio. This visit is not only a very important diplomatic milestone, but it also reflects the excellent moment that Ecuador and the United States are undergoing jointly with our administrations; and overall, it is a very clear example that we are sharing a common vision – a vision that is focused on security; that is focused on liberty, on democracy, and overall on shared prosperity. I would like to structure my presentation in three axes, which is something that we constantly work with the United States. One is the issue related to safety – our shared safety and security, focused on fighting against transnational threats, and also the threats that we are confronting right now are not only local; they know no boundaries. And in the same way we do need to tackle them in a way that is multinational and coordinated not only locally. Ecuador has assumed a very firm, brave, and decisive role in the region to try to break down these criminal organizations and drug-dealing bands that try to cause harm to our families and to our peace and to our institutions. Therefore, technical operation and political support are fundamental parts of the puzzle for this effort, and today we want to restate that the institutional strength and the exchange of intelligence, the strengthening of our capabilities, are the only way forward in order to be able to bring back the absolute peace for our peoples. Secondly, I would also like to mention the issue related to economy. Sustainable peace cannot be sustained only through security and safety, but it is also very necessary to have economic development, employment, and real opportunities for our people. Therefore, Ecuador has positioned itself as a strategic partner that is trustworthy, that opens the door for hemispheric trade in different sectors in order to be able to jointly work with the United States of America. And finally, the third axis I would like to sum up: that this is a partnership not only at the diplomatic level, and it’s not a short-term partnership; our relationship with the United States is envisioned to be lasting because our nations go beyond a simple political moment. They share democratic values and the commitment for the well-being of our nations. This visit on behalf of Secretary Rubio allows us to create a pragmatic roadmap, and a very ambitious roadmap, for the upcoming years, ensuring that our political dialogue can be translated into tangible results for each and every one of our citizens and our region. Dear Secretary, your presence here in our Ecuadorian soil really ratifies that not only are we working hand in hand, but also that we are working for a better future for both nations. Be confident that in us you will find a country that is a loyal ally, an active ally, and a decisive ally to be able to build a safer hemisphere, a free hemisphere, and prosperous hemisphere. Thank you very much. MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much, dear Foreign Minister. Now we would like to invite the intervention of Marco Rubio, the Secretary of State of the United States of America. SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much for this opportunity to be here with you again. A year and three days ago I came; this is my second official visit as the Secretary of State, and my third visit, because I came as a senator before as well. And we will see ourselves in September for sure once again, or in – even closer than next September. And thank you very much for this opportunity. The partnership between the United States and Ecuador – I’m going to share some words in English as well, just so that people don’t get offended with me, as well for my press, English-speaking press that we have from the United States. But first of all I would like to say that this partnership between – of our countries is very important. We do not have a better ally in the region with regards to confronting the big threat of criminal transnational organizations. It’s criminal transnational organization that has changed over the last few years. We had been used to criminal groups that cooperated within a national boundary, but now we see networks of terrorist organizations. Let’s not call them criminal groups; they’re terrorist groups that are attacking country after country, threatening the state, the well-being, the health, and the safety of our people. And in order to be able to discuss transnational issues we have to create a coalition of countries. And one of the countries that has participated most actively and is doing the most to confront this is Ecuador, and that’s why we’re here with you today. And we’re doing a lot of things together. Our elite forces are working jointly on a day-to-day basis in a way that has no precedence in order to try to dismantle these terrorist organizations which are causing so much harm to this country, to our country, and to plenty of other countries in our region. At the same time, we have worked – and I’m going to ask the United States Congress for 45 additional million dollars – to continue contributing towards this effort of dismantling these terrorist groups and finishing with them once and for all. At the same time, we are launching a $10 million effort in order to be able to tackle illegal mining that is stealing the riches of your country. They should be towards the benefit of people, not towards the benefit of a terrorist group. And we will also start with that initiative. I want to announce that we are giving a fleet from the U.S. Coast Guard here to Ecuador so that they are able to use it. It’s a 110-feet vessel. And on top of that, we will transfer five more interceptor vessels in the upcoming months. We will have a total of 12 total vessels – 12 of them – over the last year. And we also want to say that the results are evident. You have been able to have your interventions and have been able to see a historical numbers of seizures of drugs over the last year, which is something that was previously never before seen. I must say that as part of the effort, the administration of – President Trump’s administration has sanctioned 15 entities – criminal organizations, terrorist organizations, and also two individual people. And we have identified 10 commercial fishing companies, and we – that were also participating in illegal actions. And this is very important; we continue working on this. And today, we have made the decision on behalf of the United States Government to designate Los Tiguerones as another terrorist group, and this is on top of the things that we have done with Los Choneros and with Los Lobos and other groups that are not coming up to my mind at this point in time. But yeah, it was the three additional groups, and today with the Tiguerones as well. These criminal groups – and I’m going to repeat what I said before because it’s very important for us to highlight this. We’re not talking about mafia, normal mafia. We’re not talking about criminals. We’re talking about terrorists – terrorists that in many cases have weapons and equipment that is very similar to those from armies of certain countries. These are not common groups. They participate in common crime, of course, but they have capabilities beyond that. They’re terrorist groups. And that is something that we have to confront, we have to dismantle, and we have to beat them. And we are fully committed for that. At the same time, we have also worked on economic issues. There’s huge economic opportunities. The number one responsibility of government is the safety of the people in the country, but beyond that we do need to have prosperity, economic opportunities. And there are huge economic opportunities. Your economy is growing. It’s growing at a very impressive level, but it could even take that step further. It could accelerate even further for the benefit of the people. And we are trying to find what opportunities exist, and we know that there’s plenty of them so that United States economy and Ecuadorian economy can participate jointly to create this prosperity, which would help both countries. So with all of this, we are fully committed – 100 percent committed – and I wanted to come here as part of this official visit to add this and to keep on working on all of these things, and to have very concrete achievements like the ones we have obtained over the last year. Because oftentimes, when you come on these visits, we say and we talk about what we will do, but we have already done things, and we will even work harder. And hopefully next time we’re here we will have many more achievements that we can talk about, and also we will still have a lot to do. So thank you very much for that, and I’m going to share a couple of words in English. (In English) Just in English, first of all, I want to thank the foreign minister; I want to thank President Noboa and their administration. They’ve been incredible partners. They’re a key leader in the Shield of the Americas and in the Counter Cartel Coalition, the American – Americas Counter Cartel Coalition. In fact, they are the most involved and aggressive partner we have in that regard. Our – as we speak right now, our elite forces are operating jointly, going after criminal groups, dismantling narco networks, and bringing people to justice that had never been brough to justice before. And I think it’s important to point for a second that the groups we are taking on, these are terrorist organizations. These are not just criminal organizations. These are not just narco organizations. These are terrorist organizations. They have to be confronted, and they have to be dismantled. And that’s what we’re working on together in a way that really has no precedent, and we’re going to be doing more. For example, we’ll be asking Congress for another $45 million of new commitments to help Ecuador, working with us, to take this effort on. We’re going to be asking for $10 million as well, or we’re going to be launching an initiative – $10 million of approved projects to go after illegal gold mining and gang recruitment and illicit finance and land and maritime drug trafficking. I’m pleased to announce today that, as part of this effort, we’ll be delivering a 110-foot U.S. Coast Guard cutter to Ecuador so that that will help strengthen their navy and their ability to stop maritime narcotic trafficking and weapons shipments and illegal fishing, and a range of other threats. And we’re going to do more than just that. Next month, we’ll be transferring five more interceptor vessels. That’ll bring to a total of 12 this year – 12 this year. Again, the progress we’ve made on this relationship really has no historic precedent, and there’s so much more to do. And the results are there. You see it already. I was just told this before we got here today that the Ecuadorian navy has seized 2.5 metric tons of cocaine using these vessels that we were able to provide. They’re doing their part, and we’re going to continue to do ours. By the way, we’ve sanctioned a network of 15 entities and individuals and identified 10 commercial fishing vessels as blocked property. These are things that were being used to facilitate narcotrafficking and other things. Now, today we’ll be designating a new group and another group as a Foreign Terrorist Organization, a group known as Los Tiguerones . And this comes on the heels of our designation of three other groups, including Los Lobos and Los Choneros, in July. These are organizations – as I said, they’re not ordinary. These are violent, bloodthirsty terrorist organizations, and we have to make sure that we continue to pursue them. And as we dismantle these terrorist organizations, we also have to go after corrupt officials that collaborate and conspire with these terrorists. We’ll be announcing the designation of seven former members of the government here, officials, for accepting bribes and for betraying their most essential duties on behalf of – and they did this on behalf of these terrorist organizations, these dangerous criminal groups. There was so much more for us to do. We’ve signed a bilateral critical minerals framework earlier this year to collaborate on price challenges and to spur development. We’re going to kick off our Millennium Challenge Corporation Compact with Ecuador. We’re providing a 12 million grant to the Government of Ecuador for this compact, which is going to benefit the electricity sector and your economy. And in the end, obviously the most important obligation any government has is the safety and security of their people. But upon that foundation is where you build the foundation of prosperity and economic opportunity. Ecuador actually has economic growth, and it’s pretty impressive given some of the things that are going on around the world. But they can do so much more if the security situation gets solved – and it is being solved very aggressively – and if we work together to pursue these opportunities to jointly develop our respective economies in ways that are mutually beneficial for both countries. So thank you very much. Muchísimas gracias . MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much, Secretary. We would like to thank the presence of the authorities, the representatives of the press, and also of everybody that has been here with us today. We would like to specially request the press to please stay in your position until the authorities leave. Good afternoon, everybody, and thank you. title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori at a Joint Press Availability
text: hide Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori at a Joint Press Availability Remarks Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Keiko Fujimori, Peruvian President Presidential Palace Lima, Peru September 10, 2026 MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Welcome to the Túpac Amaru Hall of the Government Palace. Next, we will hear the remarks of the President of the Republic Keiko Sofía Fujimori Higuchi and the Secretary of State, His Excellency Marco Rubio. They will give their remarks after the meeting they held in the framework of the official meeting. Next, we’ll listen to the remarks by the President of the Republic, Ms. Keiko Sofía Fujimori. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) Good morning, Secretary of State Mr. Marco Rubio, ministers, high officers, journalists. Your presence in Peru, Secretary Rubio, represents much more than an official visit. It symbolizes the meeting of two nations which for 200 years share the same view about freedom, independence, and sovereignty. Two hundred years ago Peru started to build its republic. The United States were already consolidating it. We were two young nations but with a very strong aspiration, that America could decide about its own destiny. Two hundred years have gone by and that vision is still in force, with different nuances, aspects, and new challenges, but with the same aim: that no external force takes away from us the possibility of living in freedom. For that reason, the first topic of our meeting has been how to face transnational organized crime, and we have talked about citizenship and security. As president of the Republic of Peru, I am happy to inform our nation that Peru will become part of the Shield of the Americas – (applause) – a multilateral coalition that includes more than 15 countries and which is led by the United States. Thank you, Secretary Rubio, for this opportunity because we have had to face terrorism and we know how difficult it is to face these criminal organizations that do not respect any borders. And for this reason, we need to join efforts with other countries. Being part of the Shield of the Americas will enable us, as we have already proved, to obtain faster information and act more firmly. And from Peru, we will act with all the powers granted by the law and the constitution. We have also had the chance to talk about the challenge posed by the El Niño phenomenon. We were sharing with Secretary Rubio that this phenomenon will begin, it was announced, in February; however, the previous government did not take pertinent actions. In the first days of August, as the press already knows, we began with the cleaning of the riverbeds and prepare ourselves for the emergency. And we would like to take the opportunity to thank the United States for the support that is being provided thanks to the coordinations of Ambassador Navarro. And we are thankful because in February 2027, the Comfort American ship will arrive to the coast of Peru. This is one of the largest hospital vessels of the world, with more than 1,000 beds and highly equipped technology. This will help the population of the northern part of our country. We thank for the assistance that could be given by the Southern Command and the support that we are already receiving from the DEA and the FBI and other federal agencies. We’ve been able to talk about many subjects – education, infrastructure investment, our trade exchange. But we salute today the political decision of President Trump to look at Latin America that Secretary Rubio is here in Peru because it shows the true value you’re giving to this bilateral relations. We’re talking about 200 years of friendship. Welcome, Secretary Rubio. (Applause.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We thank the words of President of the Republic. Now we have the remarks from the Secretary of State, our Excellency Marco Rubio. SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much, dear President, for having a meeting. The cooperation that exists through the first 40 days of your administration has meant a lot. We’ve done a lot, but we will do more. I think that I come and I leave with a lot of confidence that the relations between our countries will start a very special era and will benefit both countries in a very important way. It’s important to have, like you’ve said, the relation for more than 200 years between our countries. We are a very, very young republic. You were starting as a republic; and we’ve done a lot during these 200 years, but we still have a lot to do. We are facing the modern threats, which are different from a decade ago, those new (inaudible) threats. Our obligation, the most important thing, is to achieve peace, to achieve security of the people. And when that is threatened, it’s impossible. It’s impossible to have economy growth, prosperity. It’s impossible to achieve other things if peace, calm, and order are not present. These are important things and are very necessary for economic growth and prosperity, which is all – what we want. Which is the biggest threat? The threat nowadays are transnational organized crime. Bear in mind that we had these groups operating within national territories only, but nowadays it is a network, it’s a terrorist network, a criminal network, which is very dangerous, operating through borders and multiple countries with liaisons. It’s a criminal infrastructure with banking, finance, and they’re trying to take this hemisphere. We cannot let this happen. The only way we can confront them is to be strong and confront them. This is why we’re very happy and – well, that you have been elected. People elected you because you promised to confront this, and we will provide the support. Why? Not only because of the friendship, because it’s only of our national interest. To have operating criminals operating in this hemisphere – it’s a direct threat not only for the Peruvian people, but as well for the United States. I’m very, very happy to listen to the announcement that you will be partner of the Shield of the Americas. A shield against what, people may wonder? A shield against these criminal bands, criminal groups, terrorist groups that are a direct threat to the sovereignty to our countries. When we are encountering criminal bands that have more money and best military equipment than the military themselves, that is not acceptable. And against that is the shield. This is why we have 14 countries working together – hopefully we will add more countries – to confront and defeat forever these elements. What can we do at the same time for security, prosperity? And this is why we will always seek trade opportunities to work together with your government and your country, to seek trade agreements that will benefit directly our people, and as well, the United States economy. And we have multiple possibilities. We have spoken about that today and we still have a lot to do. And we’re starting to work on those topics. So for us, it is an honor to be here with you today and to start this new era in the relations between Peru and the United States. I think we have the possibility in our hands to start a very important time, historical era, in terms of what we can achieve together. If I may please switch to English because I do have U.S. press covering this. (In English) (Inaudible) President Fujimori for receiving us here today. I truly believe that we are entering a new era in U.S.-Peru relations, a golden era in many ways, because her administration has the right ideas. In her first 40 days in office, we’ve already done many things together, and there’s so much more for us to do together. I remind everybody that the most important obligation of any government to its people is the security and the stability and the order in that country. And when that is threatened, nothing else is possible – not economic growth, not prosperity, not upward mobility. And in fact, we look at the criminality that exists and the terrorism that exists in this region today – and the people most victimized by it are working people, common people, who cannot defend themselves against these criminal elements. This is – this has always been a threat in this region. But it has become a new threat because these are now transnational threats. These are transnational terrorist organizations that do not respect sovereign borders and operate in multiple countries with the same aim and the same goal of exploiting countries and exploiting their people and harming them. And I’m very pleased to hear the announcement that Peru will be joining the Shield of the Americas. What is it a shield against? It is a shield against these threats to the sovereignty of these independent nations. It is a shield against these transnational criminal groups that, in many cases, have more money and better military equipment than the states. That is unacceptable, and the only way to defeat it is to confront it forcefully. And it’s the reason why President Fujimori was elected because she told the people of this country she would confront this threat and she would defeat it, and we will help her. We are going to help as we possibly can because it is in our national interest as well. Beyond that, there is extraordinary commercial opportunities. We’ve talked about some of those today. There are real opportunities to us to work together on commercial deals and commercial projects that are extraordinarily beneficial to Peru, to the people of Peru, but also beneficial to the people of the United States. That will be a core of our relationship as well. So it’s an honor to be here. It’s an honor to be with you. And I thank you and I thank your team for receiving us. I can’t wait to see the exciting things we’ll do together. Thank you. (Applause.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We thank our Secretary of State for his remarks. Now we will take two questions per country for each authority. Please we’d like to invite the press. Start with the name of your organization. QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Good afternoon, President and Secretary of State. My first question is for you. What is the importance of this meeting that you have sustained with the Secretary of State, considering that this first official encounter with the United States of America? And number two, what is the importance that Peru becomes part of the Shield of the Americas, and how this will strengthen the security policy in favor of Peruvians? Thank you. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) For Peru, it is of the essence – it is of the essence for Peru to know that the United States has now a political view of Latin America. We were speaking with Secretary Rubio that in previous administrations that importance was not given to the region. And his presence marks this difference – President Trump’s view. Entering the Shield of the Americas is of the essence for Peru. First of all, because it relaunches the joint work of both countries (inaudible) during the ‘90s. Let’s remember that the USA helped us in the fight against drug trafficking, and we were able to reduce the coca leaf production. In 1990 we had 120,000 hectares; that went down to 20,000 hectares. This reduction was possible with the work done with alternative crops, directly working with the farmers themselves. We have already shown results when two countries have a political decision, can work jointly shoulder to shoulder. Entering the Shield of the Americas will help us to obtain information. Peru confronted Shining Path and the MRTA, two terrorist groups, and was able to defeat them. And these two groups worked within Peruvian territory. Now criminal organizations know no borders. Some weeks ago it was possible to capture a criminal from the Los Pulpos criminal organization, and he was in Bolivia. This information was handed over to us through the FBI, and the Peruvian and Bolivian police were able to work jointly. For this reason it is of the essence to be part of the Shield of the Americas, because we will be able to act directly on our own behalf and on behalf of the cabinet of ministers led by Mr. Galarreta. We have the will to confront them, and with information from all countries we will be able to act faster and obtain specific and tangible results. QUESTION: Vera Bergengruen with The Wall Street Journal . Mr. Secretary, you have stressed that the members of the Shield of the Americas are sovereign partners. But if one of these governments refuses to act against one of these groups that Washington deems a terrorist threat, does the U.S. reserve the right to act unilaterally, including here in Peru? And President Fujimori: (Via interpreter) The question wanted more information about the partner of the Shield of the Americas. This will include to collaborate with the United States here in the country. SECRETARY RUBIO: I’ll answer that question in English to Spanish. I don’t know if you guys heard it. Basically, the gist of the question is, if you’re a member of the Shield and refuse to act, does the United States – will the United States act unilaterally? Well, if we were going to act unilaterally, why would we need the Shield? We’re not – if we were interested in acting unilaterally, we have the capacity to act unilaterally. The reason why we’re not doing it is because we want to do it with our partners. It’s the most effective way to do it. For us to confront transnational criminal groups, we need to do it inside the sovereign territory of countries, and we want to partner with those countries. It’s in their interest to do it. That is why we have the Shield. That is why the Shield exists. People make up these problems that don’t exist. They’re getting ahead of themselves with these – these ridiculous sort of things that no one’s even contemplating. The bottom line is the reason why we have a Shield is because we choose to act in partnership with our partners. So it’s very simple. This is not very complicated; let me explain this to you. It’s a very, very simple equation. We have a country that says we want to defeat these criminals, these terrorists, these evil, despicable human beings; we want to defeat them. We want to work with America to defeat them. And so we say, of course we want to work – what should we say to them? No, we don’t want to work with you? No, we’d like you not to do anything about these groups? We have a president here who has said very clearly – not to us, to the people of her country; it’s why they elected her – I am going to defeat these groups that extort you, I am going to defeat these groups that kill you, I am going to defeat these groups that terrorize your children in our communities. And the United States has said we’re so happy you’re doing that, it’s important for us as well, and we’re going to partner with you. That is the purpose of the Shield, to shield the region against this threat to the sovereignty of every one of our nations. (Via interpreter) The question was if the United States will act unilaterally if the member country of the Shield will not act. It’s a ridiculous question because if we’re going to do it unilaterally, then why would we have the Shield? The reason why we have the Shield is because we don’t want to act unilaterally. We want to act together. We want to act jointly. Why do we want it? It’s very simple. These are terrorist groups. Please be clear, these are not criminals stealing a bank. These are terrorist groups extorting people, extorting and doing a lot of – committing multiple crimes, things that you cannot even think about. They’re evil. So these – we need to defeat them, and we need to work together. When we see that there is a leader, a president that was elected with that promise to the people – and she is compliant with this; she will defeat and confront these groups – we will support her. Because it’s of our interest as well to work with you, of course, to your country or a sovereign country. And this is an enormous responsibility to confront these groups, and we will do our best to support to be able so she can comply with that promise. She will help us, but we will help them as well. This is how the partnerships work, this is how allies work, and this is what is the Shield. It is a powerful partnership against these diabolic groups that have terrorized the region for many, many years and through multiple leaders, and many, many, many political leaders from multiple countries don’t have the courage to confront them, or at many times they were involved. And this impunity will no longer be accepted, and this is what we are seeing, and in other countries as well that are a member of the Shield of the Americans. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) I want to reflect on a question. When we requested powers, this request was filed with congress by the prime minister. We requested to declare these criminal groups as hostile and terrorist groups. This mechanism will be fundamental. Second of all, we want to coordinate and strengthen the justice administration system to face decisively these criminal organizations. All of these mechanisms will help us obtain information through the Shield of the Americas and the different government agencies. (In English) So we are extremely happy, and we are thankful for Peru to be part now of the Shield of the Americas. QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Ayrton Luera from ATV Noticias . My question was with this incorporation of Peru into Shield of Americas, Mr. Rubio, would be – will we expect military operations or emergency operations in Peruvian territory? And if so, Madam President, could you tell us about the conversations that have taken place, if these interventions respect Peruvian sovereignty? And Mr. Rubio, what would be your answer to this public response of the Chinese embassy after your column in the press? SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) I don’t know what the Chinese embassy said. I’m not here to talk about what the Chinese embassy said. So, but the first question that you asked, we’re going to be – this is a sovereign country. You have your laws, you have a process. It’s a democratic country. You have a system, government system, a legal system; you will comply to that. We’re willing to do all what we can to assist you. This is going to be based on the cooperation that you request. We don’t want to be less, offer less, but not offer more than what you’re requesting. We’ll work together with this government that has an interest in defeating and have an obligation it’s committed to confront and defeat these criminal groups. So we’re not going to do anything that is outside the legal framework of your country or outside what the government will request. (In English) The question was would we do anything in the country, military activities and the like – we’re not going do anything that our partners don’t ask us to do. This is a democracy. This is a republic. They have laws, they have a system of government, they have regulations, they have a process they have to go through. We are not – we don’t want to do less than what you ask of us, but we’re not going to do more than what you ask of us. We are partners and we are allies. That’s how partnerships and alliances work. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) I wanted to mention that even before we entered the Shield of the Americas our police force was being trained by the FBI. Even Great Britain was assisting us in this training and in the strengthening of our police force. And with our entry into the Shield of Americas we will have a more solid position. With regard to the entry of troops, there is a special provision in the constitution. Every time there is this kind of entry, a special authorization is requested to the congress of the republic. Of course, we will uphold this rule. Peru’s sovereignty is intact. We will recover order, tranquility, and peace for all of the Peruvian people. For this reason, we thank Secretary Rubio for his presence and to be here to be able to announce that Peru will be part of the Shield of the Americas. Thank you so much. MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We will now listen to the last question of this conference. QUESTION: Eric Martin with Bloomberg News. Secretary Rubio, as you get ready to conclude this three-day visit to Peru, Colombia, and Ecuador, what is your message to the people of the region about the benefits of partnering with the U.S. and to voters in neighboring Brazil as they face elections in one month from now in some of the same security and other challenges of countries in the region? And President Fujimori – Presidente Fujimori: (Via interpreter) After the visit of Secretary Rubio — SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Oh, he spoke Spanish. You’re tricky. (In English) I didn’t know he spoke Spanish. (Via interpreter) I can no longer speak Spanish because he’ll know. (In English) I’m sorry. QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Thank you, Secretary. President Fujimori, after the visit of Secretary Rubio, after today, and after being six weeks in office, are you prepared to take more steps to associate and work with the United States despite the massive investment of China in Peru during the last years, including the Port of Chancay? Thank you. SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you. He speaks Spanish. I mean, I was – I’m no longer going to be able to speak Spanish in front of you. It’s a joke, obviously. First, what’s our message? Let’s be clear on this. I’ve said for more than 20 years, unfortunately, administrations of both political parties, they’ve ignored the region. The focus was on different parts of the world. If you study – because I have two jobs: Secretary of State and also I am a consultant to the national security for President Trump at the Security Council. So our National Security Strategy speaks very openly about we will give priority to this side of the hemisphere. Why? Because we’re part of it, because geography is real, and the problems of the hemisphere impacts directly. It doesn’t mean that other problems outside this hemisphere are not important, but what really happens here in South America, Central America, and the Caribbean has a direct impact to the United States. Number two, we have a lot of people in common. How many U.S. Americans come visit, have businesses here, are tourists, live here, and vice versa? We have very – a very strong bond we cannot ignore, so we’ll give the priority. And not rhetorically – because there has been other administrations, oh, no, yes, we are focused on the side of the hemisphere, but they are not doing things, they haven’t done things. We are going to be focusing. First, it’s important for us, Peru as a country, as part of our national interest. So this visit is not unexpected. I’ve done this visit as a senator, I’m doing this as the Secretary of State, and we will continue doing this type of visits, and we will have concrete efforts. It’s not just simply the Shield of the Americas. We’ll have other efforts jointly to confront the interests that we have in common with our friends and our allies. And we want all the time – this is the most important. This is very, very important in democracy. When a president is elected and the president decides to cooperate and work with the United States, it’s super important that we can show the people that there are benefits for the people to get a partnership with the United States and work together, not only at the security level but as well trade and economically speaking. And we need to try to do that, and we want to make sure that the countries that cooperate with us are going to be able to respond to their voters: This is the consequence, the result of our cooperation with the United States. (In English) Very briefly, the question was in English: What is our message? Our message is what we’ve been saying all along. We have a National Security Strategy. I helped write it. And it talks about how the Western Hemisphere is a priority for this administration – not a rhetorical priority, not a symbolic priority, not a ceremonial priority – a real priority. That’s why I’ve traveled extensively in the region, that’s why we’ve received visitors from the region, and that’s why we’re here today. Because geography is real. The things that happen in this hemisphere directly impact us. We’re not doing anybody a favor here. Us getting involved in the region is not a favor; it is essential to our own security, to our own prosperity, to our own well-being in the United States of America. And this administration is committed to this. And there’ll be more if – people talk about the Shield of the Americas. I’m very proud of it. There’s going to be more initiatives like that in multiple realms where we can work together. But for this administration, this hemisphere is a priority, and you will continue to see it demonstrated over and over and over again. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) Peru is part of APEC, the Asian Pacific economic forum; the United States too. And Peru has a significant production of minerals, fish products, agricultural products, and we will continue with this effort of having trade exchanges with different countries from Asia, from the Pacific, and from Europe of course. But today, with the presence of Secretary Rubio and the agreement signed in recent days, and with this direct collaboration that will be reciprocal, we begin a new era of relations between Peru and the United States. And these relations will surely strengthen both countries. So thank you, Secretary Rubio, for your presence. We hope you can visit us again. And we have already talked about other dates where we will be able to exchange more ideas and re-establish this cooperation, bridges between both countries. Thank you. (Applause.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We would like to thank the press for their questions, and we would like to invite President Fujimori and Secretary Rubio to step up for an official photograph. We hope that you can move forward to be able to capture this photo. This act has ended. Thank you for your presence. We wish you a good afternoon, and we will now like to request the Peruvian press to remain in your places while we wait for the other part of the press to leave. Thank you. title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the National Order of Merit in the Grade of Grand Cross Ceremony
text: hide Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the National Order of Merit in the Grade of Grand Cross Ceremony Remarks Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Palacio de Carondelet Quito, Ecuador September 9, 2026 MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Good afternoon. With your authorization, Mr. President, we will begin with the ceremony of the decoration at the grade of Grand Cross for the Order of National Merit to Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America; reading the executive decree of the conferral of the decoration of the Order of Merit, the order of Grand Cross, to Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States. FOREIGN MINISTER KURY: (Via interpreter) Executive decree 492, issued by Mr. Daniel Noboa Azín, President of the Republic: Considering that according to Article 416 of the constitution of the republic establish that the interest of the presidents of the republic will respond to the interest of the international community, and hereby decrees that integration, cooperation, and solidarity; that with (inaudible) 391 of September 17, 1920 – 2026 issued for the Order of Merit, created of – in this year, is of Article 6 of (inaudible) 0924 of 17 – of September 17, 2026 – determined that Mr. President of the Republic, through the Ministry of the Foreign Affairs, establish the way the conferral of decoration must be done. That executive decree of September 17, 2026 established that within the numerals of Article 26 have to be the minimal requirements for the conferral of decoration without prejudice; that in each case the Ministry of Foreign Affairs determines the possibility of its conferral according to the merits and the background of each candidate. Article 8 of executive decree 2026 – of 17 September 2026, establish the reasons that are not established within these numerals will be decided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs that is contained within the list above, according to the order and merits. This is an order established by the Ecuadorian state for people with a high trajectory of work and with the cooperation and friendship relations with international community in benefits of security, development, and the security of its peoples. Mr. Marco Antonio Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America, has been providing distinguished services and has done high commitment to the bonds of friendship with the Republic of Ecuador and the United States; contributed within his high functions the consolidation of a bilateral relation based on trust, cooperation, and the achievement of mutual interest; and also strengthening bilateral cooperation to face, in a coordinated way, threats coming from the transnational organized crime, in particularly narco-traffic, narco-terrorism, and networks linked to illicit economies and their funds, thus fighting against the insecurity for these institutionally and development of the Republic of Ecuador. His efforts for strengthening bilateral cooperation and security, strengthen institutional capabilities, and fight against illicit economies has contributed to have mutual agenda that has transcended these national borders, reaffirming the commitment of both countries for security, peace, stability, and the benefits of its peoples. And within the attributions conferred within the articles above mentioned, of article of September 17, 2026 decrees – hereby decrees to confer decoration to merit in the Order of Grand Cross to Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America, for his distinguished services and his strengthening of the links of friendship, cooperation between the Republic of Ecuador and the United States of America. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is here charged to execute this executive decree and the organization of the political meeting that is here, and this decree will enter into force without prejudice of its publication in official registry; given at the National Palace on September 9th, 2026, signed by Mr. Daniel Noboa Azín. (Applause.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you, Mr. Minister of Foreign Affairs. Hereby the imposition of the decoration in the Order of National Merit, in the grade of Grand Cross, to Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America, imposed by Mr. Daniel Noboa Azín, Constitutional President of the Republic. (The medal was presented.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Now, words of Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America. SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) First, thank you so much. This is a great honor for me. I’m going to go back to Washington wearing this. I’m honored to come back to visit all of you here. I was here recently and the relations with the United States and Ecuador have improved in the last years and specifically in the last three or four years, the cooperation we have on the issue of security and on the issue of prosperity, because both issues are important. However, the main goal of the government, it’s the security of this people, and when we see threats to its security, we have to work, and your president’s doing so in an incredible way. And we have seen that in every single work that we have done together. We have the same principles, and that is why we will continue to see a strong commitment on part of President Trump and our administration to help you all to continue working. At the same time, security is space for prosperity, that wants every government to have prosperity for its people, that have economic opportunities based on the help of the presidents and the authorities. So let us all know that we are here, again, at the second time, and it’s the third time that I’ve met with the president – once before in the United States – to continue showing the cooperation and the links that are between our two countries. And I once again thank you so much for this, and thank you, all of you, for being here, for receiving me and working with me and my team. And I don’t need a prize for this work; however, it is great honor to receive this. So thank you so much. (Applause.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you, Mr. Secretary. Now, the speech of Mr. Daniel Noboa Azin, Constitutional President of the Republic. PRESIDENT NOBOA: (Via interpreter) Mr. Secretary of State, in the name of the Ecuadoran people, it is the honor of us to confer the decoration in the Order of Grand Cross to the merit, the equivalent of the presidential conferral decoration in the United States. It’s not only for issue of security (inaudible) and policies and social works, but also in the culture. The details of – I’m always happy of both decorations, and in this last part, I would like to highlight, because what we will continue doing with Mr. Secretary Rubio is take care in preserving the culture of the American continent, saving its values, and giving peace not only for the United States but all the entire region. With this same strength and drive with which he’s working in his congressional hearings, he goes through every country to improve the livelihood of the peoples looking for security, safety, and also helping the United States to have a real connection not only at the level of governments but with its people. That makes him a different secretary of what’s normally. He’s special. Moreover, that is known worldwide, that he’s solved many problems that are hard to solve. There he is, Mr. Marco Rubio, solving each problem, knowing that even if that problem doesn’t have a solution, Mr. Marco Rubio will find a solution. (Applause.) He has led very differently of what’s normal. That makes him to have a good relation of the United States to the world and highlights also his roots and the connection with Latin America. We, from the part of Ecuador, we are always thankful with his work, his service, and we have achieved working hand in hand with the United States to provide more peace, health, and also more liberties, not only for our peoples but also for the entire continent. Once again, I would like to repeat that it’s an honor for me to grant this decoration, the highest that Ecuador has here in Ecuador, and I hope to have him many times here in Ecuador visiting us, and also accompanying us with this fight to change the continent, and it’s for once, for all. Thank you so much. (Applause.) title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks at the American Chamber of Commerce Peru Event
text: hide Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks at the American Chamber of Commerce Peru Event Remarks Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Museo De Arte De Lima Lima, Peru September 10, 2026 SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you. It is a pleasure to be here with you today in Peru. It is the second time that I am here. I came many years ago as a senator as the first time to – that I am here. We were waiting for Bernie to come. He’s doing a great job. I know of him for many years, and I am not surprised about the work that he has been doing. And I think that he is a perfect person when talking about the relation between Peru and the U.S. because it is a moment of extraordinary opportunities. First, I wanted to share what I have been saying since I came here. For me – I think not for me but for everyone, the main role of any government is security and stability. It is the most important, right? Without security, you cannot accomplish anything. And unfortunately, not only in Peru but in the region is confronting a very extraordinary threat. Usually, these threats will be – were taking place within national groups. What has changed in the world, what has changed in the region, is that these groups are now transnational, operating from Colombia against Peru, operating in Peru against Bolivia, operating in Bolivia against Ecuador. So a huge threat. And the only way of dealing with this or confronting these groups, if we don’t confront them and defeat them, they will eat the country. This is very Cuban. I don’t know how you translate it, but yeah. They will – they will just impact the society. And who will suffer the most? The working class, of course. They are being blackmailed, extortion – they are paying the price. But not only because of the sovereignty of a country; if your territory is controlled by criminal groups, by terrorist groups, how can you be protecting? And I’m happy that you have an administration with President Fujimori that is committed to confront these delinquents, these criminals, and we will provide the support that she needs. This is not just simply to help Peru and help her. It is also to help ourselves, because these terrorist groups are a threat to Peru but are also a threat to the United States and to the North American people. Without security, you don’t have prosperity. Obviously, there are a lot of things that we need to do for prosperity. There are companies that don’t like to invest in a country where you don’t feel safe. But also, you need to have security, legally due process – the due process. This is how you attract foreign investment. This is what we want to see. It’s logic that the United States and Peru have relations and very strong bonds and very close in terms of trade, and for us that is a priority as well. It is possible to work on security and at the same time work on trade, of course, and these are related. And it is a priority for this administration, a priority for President Trump. He is a businessman; he is not a political man. He started, yeah, in politics 10 years ago, but clearly he’s not political. He is a businessman, and this is what he understands and he appreciates. And we want to see more trade activity between Peru and the U.S., and there are great opportunities in order to do so. I’d like to tell you that what we give you are two things. Number one, unfortunately, well, political instability in Peru. As a Secretary, I think we have had to deal with three different administrations in a year and a half. And it’s impressive because usually you have two presidents in 10 years. But now we have stability, and I think that is important. But also, there has been some negligence from the government, from both political parties in the U.S., that have said, no, yeah, the hemisphere, South America, everything is important; the Americas are important for us. They all said this, but few do something about it. And we are doing something about this. For us, it is a priority. (Applause.) Why? Why is it a priority? Well, first, because of geography. It is logic that we are going to have trade exchanges. I’d rather have those exchanges with countries that are close to our country. Obviously we’re going to have relations, but it is obvious that we will have these type of exchanges where we have so close – where we’re so close geographically. Number two is logic because the reality is one of the things that is impacting manufacturing – access to critical minerals, access to all of these elements. It’s easy to have a source of these minerals that it is on the same hemisphere instead of bringing this from Africa. This doesn’t mean that we’re not interested in Africa or Asia, but the logic thing to do is to have access to these minerals, to production, and the production capability of countries that are close to our nation. Logistically speaking, it’s easier. Number two, this is not a region that has a war. You’re fighting a war against criminals, but we – you don’t have global conflicts like other countries in the world. Three, because our system and cultures are very similar. We have already connections at a banking level, at a transaction level, at a social level. And logically, because it supports the countries around the region to develop economically, and this is part of the interest of the United States. So if we have economic issues, if we have political issues, if we have social issues, unfortunately, and insecurity, this has a direct impact on the United States, and we have seen this, right? If you study the situation in Mexico that nowadays, tragically, there is territory in Mexico controlled by cartel; they are the government. But it also has an impact on the border with the U.S. and threatens the U.S. directly. So for us, if there are problems of the hemisphere, this becomes our problem as well. So for all of these reasons, it’s logic. And I know that you have representatives of many companies that for many years you have investing in the urban economy and have an American representation. We don’t only want you to continue doing this, but we want you to do more. We are coordinating very closely through the ambassador, through the embassy, with the government, and then the administration to make sure that any barrier that exists in the Peruvian system – that this has to be clear, so it makes your job easier. And then, of course, it’s part of our jobs to do more to be able to have more opportunities for the American companies in terms of the opportunity of trade and investment. We need to also play that role to support, inform through our economic bureaus to U.S. companies that are seeking to invest around the world and most likely they are not aware of Peru because we were not focused on this side of the hemisphere. This is why it’s important to be here today to thank you for all the things that you have been doing for many years. You’re here because you have been working for many years. We want you to be able to more, and we want you to have new markets, new partners, and new tools available. And please be aware that you are a priority for us, for the Department of State and from our embassy to develop all these things. I think it’ll help Peru. Without a doubt, it’ll help the United States, it’ll help you, and it’ll help the entire hemisphere. So for me, it’s been a very productive visit. I just come from the presidential palace where we had a meeting with the president and then we had a press conference. It went very well, and I hope to come back at least once before they kick out Bernie Navarro from here. I’m joking. But yeah, well, God willing, we will be able to come and we will have more things to discuss. But during the last – well, the last 40 days for the new administration, we – they requested many things and we have agreed to cooperate in many topics and we have complied and we are in a good start. We need to continue. We need to follow up on this. We need to provide continuity. We have Bernie Navarro here, focused 100 percent. He’s working every day. But he also has a direct connection with me and the White House that in a world that is experiencing so many things with Iran, with Ukraine, with Russia, with all the things that are taking place, it is important to know that you have in the U.S. system people in high positions that are focusing on this side of the hemisphere, but specifically on the relation with Peru that for many – well, more than 10 years was, like, kind of put aside. I don’t want to say abandoned. This will change. And I’d like to thank you for being patient with us, and keep being steady, firm, because we’re starting a new era. And I think it’ll be the best era in the relation between both our countries. Thank you very much. (Applause.) title: United States Welcomes Djibouti’s Signing of the Artemis Accords
text: hide United States Welcomes Djibouti’s Signing of the Artemis Accords Media Note Office of the Spokesman September 14, 2026 The Department of State congratulates the Republic of Djibouti on joining the Artemis Accords. Djibouti is the 72nd country to sign the Accords to date, pledging its commitment to the peaceful exploration of space. Djibouti’s Ambassador to the United States Mohamed Siad Douale signed the Accords on behalf of the Republic of Djibouti on September 14, 2026. NASA Deputy Administrator Matthew Anderson and State Department Assistant Secretary for African Affairs Frank Garcia witnessed and celebrated the signing at a ceremony at the Mary W. Jackson NASA Headquarters in Washington, D.C. Djibouti most recently participated in the Department’s U.S.-Africa Technical and Regulatory Space Training Meeting in April 2026, and Djibouti’s first two satellites launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base in 2023 and 2024 respectively. The United States and seven other countries established the Artemis Accords in 2020 to serve as a set of practical principles to guide responsible space exploration. Djibouti joins the United States and 70 other nations in affirming the Accords’ principles for sustainable civil space activity. The Department of State and NASA lead the United States’ outreach and implementation of the Accords. For more information, including a full list of signatories to the Accords, please visit Artemis Accords . For media inquiries, please submit a request .
